name: dns_slow
title: A slow resolver
description: Name lookups climb from 20 ms to several hundred. Pages feel slow to start even though they transfer normally once open.

card.title: This device looks like the problem
card.summary: The signals that changed are on this machine rather than on the network around it: CPU 15%, 1.3% of connections retransmitted.
remediation: Close whatever is using the most CPU or bandwidth on this device.
Restart this device's network adapter.
Check for an update to this device's network adapter driver.

evidence.label: TCP segment retransmissions divided by segments sent
system-wide CPU utilisation

card.title: The far end is slow to answer
card.summary: Your router and the path out to the internet both look normal, but the services we test are taking 79 ms to send their first byte, about 61 ms more than the network itself explains.
remediation: Check whether other sites are fine; if they are, the problem is at the far end and not with your connection.
Check the service's own status page.
Wait a few minutes; this often clears on its own.

card.title: Name lookups are slow
card.summary: Looking up addresses is taking 57 ms, well above normal for this network. DNS is the internet's phone book: when it is slow, pages feel slow to start even once they load fine.
remediation: Flush the DNS cache on this device.
Try a different DNS resolver in your network settings.
Wait a few minutes; this often clears on its own.
